speaker: narrator
text: Dark comes down on the burgomaster's house. You bar the shutters and hang garlic over every sill.

speaker: narrator
text: Wolves come out of the mist and circle the house. They do not howl. They scratch at the shutters, patient.

speaker: narrator
text: Then three knocks, and a voice at the door, soft and courteous.

speaker: count
text: Only open it. One door always opens, in the end.

speaker: narrator
text: A hunter stands and walks to the door, slow, like someone half asleep. A hand is already on the latch.

speaker: lenka
text: Don't answer him. Whatever he says, don't answer.

speaker: narrator
text: You pull them back from the door by the arms. The wolves hit the shutters all at once.

speaker: narrator
text: The last wolf runs back into the mist. The scratching stops. Lenka lets out a breath she has held for an hour.

speaker: narrator
text: You talk low and steady until the hand lets go of the latch. Outside, the voice laughs once, and goes to the village.

speaker: narrator
text: The latch lifts. Cold comes in with the mist. When the lamps steady, there is blood at a hunter's throat.

speaker: narrator
text: Down in the village, a bell rings for someone who will not wake.

speaker: narrator
text: The door slams on the mist. The wolves are gone. Lenka does not look at any of you.

speaker: narrator
text: Grey light at last. The wolves are gone, and Lenka is still with you.

speaker: narrator
text: A long hall, and a feast laid for many. Every candle is lit. Every chair is empty.

speaker: narrator
text: At the far end an organ is playing. A tall shape sits at it, its back to you.

speaker: count
text: Sit. Eat. You have come so far, and so rudely.

speaker: narrator
text: Step closer, and the bench is empty. The keys go on moving without him.

speaker: narrator
text: Behind you, the doors swing shut. Along the walls, the stone statues turn their heads.

speaker: narrator
text: They have known you were coming since the bridge. They move first.

speaker: narrator
text: The last statue breaks across the floor. The organ stops in the middle of a note.

speaker: narrator
text: A vaulted cellar under the castle, flooded to the knee. The water is black, and very still.

speaker: narrator
text: Something moves under the surface. Then something else. The water was never empty.

speaker: narrator
text: Hands come up out of the black water before you can raise a blade. The drowned dead strike first.

speaker: narrator
text: The last of them sinks back into the water, and stays down. The ripples take a long time to stop.

speaker: narrator
text: You climb back up the steps, soaked to the bone. Below, the water goes still again, and waits.

speaker: narrator
text: A crypt under the castle, low and cold. Old coffins line the walls, their lids pushed aside.

speaker: narrator
text: The lamps gutter. When they steady, one of you stands a step apart, and does not blink.

speaker: narrator
text: It wears your friend's face, and its smile is too wide. Behind the stone, someone is knocking.

speaker: narrator
text: The wight falls apart in grave dust. Your friend climbs out of a coffin behind it, cold, and alive.

speaker: narrator
text: The lamps gutter. When they steady, your companion stands a step apart. It wears their face, and smiles too wide.

speaker: narrator
text: The wight falls apart in grave dust. Your companion climbs out of a coffin behind it, cold, and alive.

speaker: narrator
text: The lamps gutter. Across the crypt stands someone in your clothes, with your own face. It smiles first.

speaker: narrator
text: It falls apart in grave dust, and your face goes with it. You are alone again, and glad of it.

speaker: narrator
text: You fall back up the stair. Behind you, something with a friend's face waits among the coffins.

speaker: narrator
text: A round room near the top of the castle. In the middle, a great heart of glass hangs on chains, beating.

speaker: narrator
text: With every beat the floor tilts. Stone grinds. The whole tower leans, and leans back.

speaker: narrator
text: Halberds rattle on their hooks. The heart beats faster, and the whole room turns on you.

speaker: narrator
text: The heart cracks, and the beating stops. The tower settles, and is still.

speaker: narrator
text: The wight turns its borrowed face toward you. The voice that comes out of it is his.

speaker: count
text: Look closely. You could not tell us apart. Soon, neither will they.

speaker: narrator
text: A hand comes out of the dark at the head of the table, palm up, held out to Lenka.

speaker: lenka
text: No. Not to you. Not ever.

speaker: narrator
text: The heart's beat turns toward Stefan's blade. Whatever the room throws, it throws at the one who carries it.

speaker: narrator
text: As you reach the top floor, every candle goes out at once. From here, you climb in the dark.
